declared.title: Intrinsic motivation and extrinsic incentives jointly predict performance: A 40-year meta-analysis.
declared.foundIn: OpenAlex search « intrinsic motivation performance meta-analysis » (2026-11-23)

population: 183 samples (212,468 people) at school, at work and in physical activities

findings.text: Weighed together with incentives, intrinsic motivation predicted the quality of performance better, while incentives better predicted its quantity

support.sentence: Considered simultaneously through meta-analytic regression, intrinsic motivation predicted more unique variance in quality of performance, whereas incentives were a better predictor of quantity of performance.

findings.text: Intrinsic motivation stayed important to performance whether or not incentives were offered

support.sentence: The importance of intrinsic motivation to performance remained in place whether incentives were presented.

limits: associations: motivation and performance mostly measured together, so performance may also raise interest
compared with extrinsic incentives, not with people who value only the result; the outcome is performance, not persistence
intrinsic motivation is interest and enjoyment, not the acceptance of pain the book speaks of
countries not listed in the abstract; no sample from the Middle East or North Africa known
